answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. This is why the network can stay open without a central gatekeeper: the economics of reputation do the filtering that a trusted authority otherwise would.. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. Consider a echo as the anchor of the cost.
